Introduction: ^Welcome to "From Noble Love, a retelling of the most scandalous trial of 1700s London and English high society...the bigamy trial of Elizabeth Cudleigh...

^The trial investigated her marriages to two English nobles, the validity of the second marriage and the supposed annulment of the first, and how all this was brought about by the disinherited Evelyn Meadows who sought to prove bigamy in order to claim what he thought was his rightful inheritance.

^This digital story is inspired by young 18-year-old Anna Larpent’s letters, a witness from the box seats in the courtroom at the time, and aims to give the perspective of one of the thousands of people who managed to get tickets for this must see event of 1776 London.
^Anna in her own words in a letter to her friend Gertrude explained how the events of this trial captured her imagination writing:...

^"A month ago I raved about chapeaux plumied (feathered hats) and fine men, I now am in love with nothing but wigs, gowns, and bands; as to Mr. Thurloe (the attorney general), I think or dream of nothing else!"...

^Let us now begin our journey into the high society drama of 1776 London, 250 years after the travails of Elizabeth Cudleigh, the Duchess of Kingston, captured the attention of the capital of the British Empire and a young Anna Larpent...
Start: ^It is April 25th, 1776. Anna Larpent takes a stroll through the English Garden in London, during a beautiful sunrise at 7 O’clock. Looking out for a special someone that called her here...
Begin: ^Anna hears a voice calling out to her, so sweet, like honeysuckle. Her head whips over to gaze at who called her and falls upon a woman dressed in off-white seated before a tea set.
^"Oh goodness! Gertrude! My dear friend, it’s been so long!"

^"I know! My travels across the British Isles have left me wanting my dear friend’s presence! I’ve heard from the grapevine that of this scandal in London that took place and you, darling, were there present to see it all revealed!"
^"Please tell me all you saw! Was Elizabeth...THE Elizabet...who was once the maid of honor of Augusta the Princess of Wales really..."
^Gertrude leans in and begins speaking in hushed tone with emphasis...
^"...really married to two men and became BOTH the Duchess of Kingston AND Countess of Bristol!!"... Anna makes eye contact with Gertrude and a knowing smirk grows on her face...
^"I must admit that I am most curious my dear Anna!"

^"But of course, Gerty, I cannot imagine another friend I would want to share this with...the drama of that courtroom was far more intriguing than e're we ever saw at those courtly balls we first debuted in society!"
^Anna takes a seat across from Gertrude and debates taking a sip of the tea set before her.
Tea: ^"Still knowing my tea preference, I see. New Jersey Tea, with two cubes of sugar."

^Gertrude nods knowingly, she wouldn’t forget her best friend’s tea combination. She takes a sip of the herbal tea, the dark roasted leaves mimicking the taste of black tea from Cathay. She clears her throat and then slams her hands on the table, standing up in the process.

^"Now enough teasing!! You know for which reason I return to the great city of London! The Great Bigamy Trial of Elizabeth Chudleigh! Such tension, such drama! Please, dear! You cannot keep me waiting for much longer!!"
edging: ^Anna smiles and holds her hand up.
^"Alright, my dear Gerty. I shan't keep you waiting. Take your seat and listen closely..."
^Taking a breath Anna composes hereself and looks to Gertrude and embraces her hand across the table giddy with excitement...
^"In this moment Gerty, no chaos ever equelled my head at present and I will venture to tell you this story of our age for which the whole town has talked of nothing else for this past week!"
Procession: ^"You may wonder how I got the tickets, it was quite lucky to make a connection with Lady Bathurst who had overflow tickets in the Lord High Steward's box in the court...for I did not have a reserved ticket and this was my only way into the room that day!"

^"I had to be up at 5 O'Clock in the morning for the hairdresser to prepare for such an event and then had to meet Lady Bathurst at the Coffee House which adjoins the House of Lords...there we had an elegant breakfast while Lady Bathurst's company of attendees gathered as we waited for the trial to begin."

^"At 10 in the morning we went into the hall for the trial and took our places in the box seats...it was quite a sight - a hall filled with well dressed people all extreamly striking in appearance as we wait for the procession to come into the hall and begin the trial!"
^"You could feel the anticipation in the room as the trial started...all 36 of us with Lady Bathurst in her box fixated on the door as it opened and the procession commenced!"

^"And so it began, for this was the first day of the trial for when the Duchess of Kingston was tried for Bigamy, April the 15th, the 16th year of the reign of our sovereign King George III, at about eleven in the morning, the procession entered..."

^"Gerty, you must suppose yourself with me in the Hall, imagine it! The procession 'twas an elegant sight indeed! First came the Lord High Steward with 20 gentlemen walking two by two and nor was it an unpleasing sight to see a number of these who we pretty, genteel, and well dressed young men..."
^"Then came the Clerks of the council...Soon followed by the Masters in chancery two by two in their gowns and bands!"
^"Then came the Judges in their lavish scarlett robes and caps!"
^"The Bishops came next, which I must say that their robes are very ungraceful...and to be honest...being mostly old men I cannot say I was charmed by any of their lordships!"
^Gertude almost spits out her tea to laugh...

^"Then came those of the highest order...walking alone, as he is a Prince of hte Blood, with his train borne, was the Duke of Cumberland followed by his herolds dressed for the ceremony in elegant robes with the coat of arms of England..."

^"Once the procession was seated, silence draped the hall and the herold announced in a booming voice calling Elizabeth in saying "We call the prisoner into the court...Elizabeth, calling yourself Duchess Dowager of Kingston to stand for your judgement!"
^"Finally came Elizabeth Chudleigh with her three ladies, all in black gowns. Elizabeth herself in a fine black silk dress with not a speck of white discerned!"
^"Elizabeth wore a long black hood which fell on her shoulders exactly as the headdress of Mary Queen  of Scots in the old pictures along with black gloves and a black fan!"
^"She seemed wholly unconcerned, seemingly unaffectedly so about the swirl of scandal surrounding her...she really looked handsome!"
^"Oh Anna you always have a way with words, it is as if I was fortunate enough to be in Lady Bathurst box seeing this drama of our time unvailed before me!"
^"At last, my dear friend, there is so much more to tell..."
